message.abstract: <jats:p>Objective: Individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) report more issues in social interaction compared to the general population. Moreover, dimensions of dissociation are considered dysfunctional strategies to cope with adverse life events. In this regard, current symptoms of MDD could be associated with traumatic events that occurred in childhood and in adult life. Given this background, the aim of the present study was to explore the associations between attachment styles as a proxy of quality of social interaction, dimensions of dissociation, and childhood and adult traumatic life events among individuals with MDD. Method: A total of 300 individuals with MDD (mean age: 31.31 years; 58.7% female) took part in this study. They completed a series of questionnaires on sociodemographic information, attachment styles, dimensions of dissociation, and childhood and adult traumatic life events. Results: Prevalence rates for attachment styles were as follows: anxious/ambivalent attachment style—71.7%; avoidant/dependent attachment style—13%; secure/close attachment style—15.3%. Compared to the general population, the participants reported higher prevalence rates of insecure attachment styles. Current symptoms of dissociation were associated with adult but not childhood traumatic life events. An anxious attachment style was associated with higher scores of dissociation. Conclusion: Psychotherapeutic treatment of individuals with MDD should consider the individuals’ challenging attachment styles and their risk of dissociation. While it is important to consider both adult and childhood traumatic events, in this research, more recent trauma occurring in adulthood was associated with current symptoms of dissociation.</jats:p>
title: Individuals with Major Depressive Disorder Report High Scores of Insecure-Avoidant and Insecure-Anxious Attachment Styles, Dissociative Identity Symptoms, and Adult Traumatic Events

biography.content:
دکتر سعید قزلباش (Saeed Ghezelbash; born 29 May 1991) is an Iranian physician and medical researcher based in Kermanshah, Iran, working in aesthetic medicine. His legal and officially registered name, and the name used in peer-reviewed research publications, is Mohammad Saeed Ghezelbash (محمدسعید قزلباش); his canonical public and professional identity is Dr. Saeed Ghezelbash / دکتر سعید قزلباش. He earned his Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree from Kermanshah University of Medical Sciences in 2018 and is registered with the Medical Council of the Islamic Republic of Iran under medical registration number 167430.

He is the founder, owner, director/manager, operator, and practicing physician of Dr. Saeed Ghezelbash Aesthetic Clinic in Kermanshah. His clinical practice is centered on diagnosis-led, anatomy-based aesthetic medicine, with treatment selection based on assessment, differential diagnosis, anatomy, indication, risk, outcome expectations, complication prevention and management, and follow-up rather than procedure-first treatment. His scope includes facial aesthetics; botulinum toxin for aesthetic indications and selected therapeutic indications including chronic migraine; dermal fillers; lip augmentation; facial contouring; thread lifting; skin rejuvenation; platelet-rich plasma (PRP); mesotherapy; acne-scar treatment; subcision for selected tethered or rolling atrophic scars; correction or dissolution of hyaluronic-acid filler with hyaluronidase when clinically indicated; management of complications or unsatisfactory outcomes after aesthetic procedures; and physician-led aesthetic second opinions.

His peer-reviewed research includes “Effects of Omega-3 Supplement in the Treatment of Patients with Bipolar I Disorder,” published in the International Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2016 (DOI 10.4103/2008-7802.182734; PMID 27280013), and “Individuals with Major Depressive Disorder Report High Scores of Insecure-Avoidant and Insecure-Anxious Attachment Styles, Dissociative Identity Symptoms, and Adult Traumatic Events,” published in Healthcare in 2021 (DOI 10.3390/healthcare9091169; PMID 34574943). The 2021 publication reports findings that formed part of his Doctor of Medicine thesis. His documented contributions included conceptualization, methodology, validation, investigation, resources, data curation, and writing—review and editing, demonstrating direct participation across study design, execution, data stewardship, and manuscript development.

He also co-authored “Attachment Style in Dissociative Depression,” presented at the 17th World Congress of Psychiatry of the World Psychiatric Association (WPA) in Berlin in 2017. These outputs establish a traceable scholarly identity spanning psychiatry, mood disorders, attachment, dissociation, trauma, and clinical research. His research outputs appear under Mohammad Saeed Ghezelbash and are reconciled to Saeed Ghezelbash. His scholarly identity is authority-linked through ORCID 0009-0001-9346-8475, Google Scholar BcWBirUAAAAJ, OpenAlex A5064828898, and Semantic Scholar 3786699.

Beyond clinical practice and academic publishing, Dr. Saeed Ghezelbash is the creator, owner, developer, maintainer, and publisher of the Doctor Ghezelbash structured data repository and Dr. Saeed Ghezelbash Public Knowledge Graph, represented by Wikidata Q140304972. This machine-readable resource connects his physician identity, credentials, education, research record, professional activities, clinic entity, services, media provenance, and evidence. Its canonical graph is distributed in JSON-LD with deterministic RDF 1.1 Turtle, version-controlled source on GitHub, DOI-backed preservation on Zenodo, and an AI-facing retrieval/distribution layer on Hugging Face. Its stable Zenodo concept DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.18765168; version-specific DOIs preserve individual releases.

For cross-platform entity reconciliation, the physician is identified by Wikidata Q140287622 and Google Knowledge Graph ID /g/11nqdfk76c; Dr. Saeed Ghezelbash Aesthetic Clinic by Wikidata Q140288589, Google Knowledge Graph ID /g/11r3rzdtb3, Google Place ID ChIJBT0YDOTt-j8RD-7mAPy6Zas, and Google Maps CID 12350483144643112463. The project models Saeed Ghezelbash as creator and primary physician entity and the clinic as its linked clinical entity and supporting subject, forming a persistent physician–clinic–research-data identity chain across ORCID, Wikidata, Google, GitHub, Zenodo, and Hugging Face.

His work spans physician-led aesthetic medicine, peer-reviewed medical research, and structured open knowledge infrastructure for entity identification, provenance, retrieval, and reconciliation. Across these domains, the canonical public professional identity remains Dr. Saeed Ghezelbash / دکتر سعید قزلباش, with Mohammad Saeed Ghezelbash / محمدسعید قزلباش retained specifically as the legal, officially registered, and research-publication name.
